statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers and clients SHOULD use standard HTTP caching mechanisms to reduce unnecessary network overhead.
actions: Apply standard HTTP caching mechanisms when serving or fetching Agent Cards

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agent Card HTTP endpoints SHOULD include a Cache-Control response header with a max-age directive appropriate for the agent's expected update frequency
actions: Include Cache-Control response header with a max-age directive appropriate for the agent's expected update frequency in Agent Card HTTP responses

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agent Card HTTP endpoints SHOULD include an ETag response header derived from the Agent Card's version field or a hash of the card content
actions: Include an ETag response header derived from the Agent Card's version field or a hash of the card content in Agent Card HTTP responses

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agent Card HTTP endpoints MAY include a Last-Modified response header
actions: Optionally include a Last-Modified response header in Agent Card HTTP responses

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD honor HTTP caching semantics as defined in RFC 9111 when fetching Agent Cards
actions: Honor HTTP caching semantics as defined in RFC 9111 when fetching Agent Cards

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a cached Agent Card has expired, clients SHOULD use conditional requests (If-None-Match with the stored ETag, or If-Modified-Since) to avoid re-downloading unchanged cards
actions: Send conditional request using If-None-Match with the stored ETag, or If-Modified-Since header to avoid re-downloading unchanged Agent Cards

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the server does not include caching headers, clients MAY apply an implementation-specific default cache duration
actions: Apply an implementation-specific default cache duration when the server does not include caching headers
